Taoiseach Micheál Martin was in Limerick this past week trying to spin the narrative, claiming that housing tenancies have actually increased. But let’s look at what's really happening on the ground when the state starts meddling in private contracts and undermining property rights. 

Ever since the Government introduced those heavy-handed new rules on March 1 forcing landlords to provide rigid six-year leases, we’ve seen a predictable disaster unfold. Instead of fostering stability, this kind of bureaucratic overreach punishes property owners and disrupts the natural order of the housing market. And what is the result of this progressive social engineering? Exactly what any sensible person with a respect for tradition and personal responsibility could have predicted: a rise in eviction notices and homelessness, with the numbers of people in emergency accommodation nationally increasing again. 

When you strip away people's independence and slap mandatory government decrees onto basic agreements between citizens, the social fabric frays and families suffer. It’s time to stop doubling down on failed interventions and start respecting the foundational pillars of property, responsibility, and common sense.

Well folks, let’s look at the absolute mess we’re in because the progressive establishment just refuses to respect basic common sense and the natural order of things. Taoiseach Micheál Martin was down in Limerick this past week trying to spin the narrative, claiming that housing tenancies have actually increased. But let’s look at what's really happening on the ground when the state starts meddling in private contracts and undermining property rights. 

Ever since the Government introduced those heavy-handed new rules on March 1 forcing landlords to provide rigid six-year leases, we’ve seen a predictable disaster unfold. Instead of fostering stability, this kind of bureaucratic overreach punishes property owners and disrupts the natural order of the housing market. And what is the result of this progressive social engineering? Exactly what any sensible person with a respect for tradition and personal responsibility could have predicted: a rise in eviction notices and homelessness, with the numbers of people in emergency accommodation nationally increasing again. 

When you strip away people's independence and slap mandatory government decrees onto basic agreements between citizens, the social fabric frays and families suffer. It’s time to stop doubling down on failed interventions and start respecting the foundational pillars of property, responsibility, and common sense.

Instead of systemic housing justice, we see a system where property owners wield disproportionate power, leading directly to a rise in eviction notices and homelessness, with the numbers of people in emergency accommodation nationally increasing again.
